forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Greater Manchester Combined Authority agrees interest-free loans for councils given capitalisation directions
news_drafts.lead:
The Greater Manchester Combined Authority has agreed in principle to provide interest-free loans to the region's local authorities if and when they become subject to capitalisation directions, government permission to treat day-to-day spending as capital spending so it can be paid for by borrowing or asset sales. The decision was taken on 27 March 2026, according to the authority's mid-year treasury management paper to its Audit Committee, which meets on 16 November 2026.

The paper describes the arrangement as "providing interest free loans to GM local authorities if and when they became subject to Exceptional Financial Support capitalisation directions." Exceptional financial support is permission from government to borrow, or sell assets, to cover day-to-day spending. The maximum loan is the lower of the permitted funding and the revenue costs capitalised. Repayment is expected by 31 March 2029 unless the date is extended.

The paper also asks the committee to approve investments of more than 365 days with those councils, because the loans would run for longer than a year.

news_drafts.headline: Greater Manchester Combined Authority's draft accounts assessed as a going concern, with a balanced budget
news_drafts.lead:
Greater Manchester Combined Authority's audit committee was told that the authority remained a going concern, meaning its accounts can be prepared on the basis that it will keep operating. The assessment supports the draft accounts, the authority's formal annual statement of its finances, and is recorded in the minutes of the committee's meeting on 22 July. The combined authority is a body run by several councils together, with a mayor, for transport and economic growth.

The minutes say the assessment rested on four things: a balanced approved budget, "strong reserve levels", multi-year funding certainty through the Integrated Settlement, and "robust financial planning arrangements". Reserves are money the authority has put aside. The papers give no figures for the reserves or the settlement.

The committee noted how thorough the assessment was. It had considered financial performance, reserves, liquidity (the cash available to meet bills as they fall due) and treasury management, which is how the authority borrows, invests spare cash and manages the risks of both.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: The Committee records the cyber threat as "heightened" and asks for integrated governance of cyber security, operational resilience and business continuity.
findings.detail: The Alert section says the Committee highlighted the need for integrated governance across cyber security, operational resilience and business continuity, to be considered at a Board-level Risk Workshop. The paper says existing resources were considered sufficient for current commitments.
findings.matters: Cyber and operational resilience governance is a growing area of due diligence for lenders and a comparison point for other public bodies.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Bus franchising disclosure requirements must be resolved before the 2025/26 accounts are signed.
findings.detail: The paper flags bus franchising as a financial reporting matter that needs resolving before sign-off. It says the resolution has to balance accounting requirements against commercial sensitivity.
findings.matters: Disclosure judgements on a major programme affect how the accounts present the authority's commitments, and finance officers at other transport and combined authorities facing franchising would weigh the same question.
findings.quote: Bus franchising disclosure requirements require resolution before the 2025/26 accounts are signed, balancing accounting requirements with commercial sensitivity.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Forvis Mazars remains confident the 2025/26 accounts audit will be completed before Christmas, subject to progress being maintained.
findings.detail: The paper says good progress has been made in rebuilding assurance and that the external auditor's confidence is conditional on progress continuing. The 2025/26 accounts audit is therefore expected to finish before the end of 2026.
findings.matters: The timing of a completed external audit affects when a council can publish audited accounts, which lenders and peer finance teams track.
findings.quote: Good progress has been made in rebuilding assurance, and Forvis Mazars remained confident that the audit will completed before Christmas, subject to progress being maintained.

findings.committee: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: The Committee called for stronger first-line ownership, earlier intervention and clearer escalation so that audit action deadlines are not missed, with a revised approach to be developed with the People Committee.
findings.detail: The paper lists audit actions as an Alert item and says a revised approach is to be developed with the People Committee and raised through the Chief Executive's Leadership Team. The overall assurance line names overdue audit actions as one of three areas needing sustained senior attention. The paper gives no count of overdue actions.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to know whether a council's audit recommendations are being closed on time, and a peer council would see how one authority is responding to slipping audit actions.
findings.quote: The Committee called for stronger first-line ownership, earlier intervention and clearer escalation when audit action deadlines to ensure audit actions deadlines are not missed.

findings.paper_title: DRAFT Auditor's Annual Report- GMCA 25-26 (updated for Steve's comments)
findings.headline: The Government's latest Devolution Deal came into effect on 1 April 2026, giving GMCA greater powers to use funding more flexibly.
findings.detail: The paper says the deal allows GMCA to plan and fund local priorities over the longer term. It does not give any financial values for the change.
findings.matters: A change in the funding flexibility of a combined authority affects how peers and lenders assess its long-term budget planning.
findings.quote: On 1 April 2026 the Government’s latest Devolution Deal came into effect.
